ana: Quick heads-up — after today's AWQ weight-only packing rollout I’m seeing a consistent tail latency regression (~8-12%) on our chat P50->P99 for int8 paths. Running on dedicated fleets, group_size=64.

mike: ugh. any smoke in profiler? kernel switch / prefetch misses?

ana: Profile points to two things: extra unpack work when packing crosses slab boundaries, and more importantly KV cache prefetch not hitting for the new pack layout. Seems like packing alignment changed prefix boundaries so our hotset predictor is missing.

sam: can you share the flamegraph? even a snippet helps.

ana: pasted a tiny tail of the perf report:

```
sampled stacks: 120s window
- runtime/awq_pack_unpack  28%
- runtime/int8_matmul_kern 22%
- kvcache/prefetch_path    18%
- scheduler/batch_wait     12%
- io/serialize             8%

note: prefetch_path misses spike during 0.5-1.0s interactions
```

chris: that matches what we saw last quarter when group_stride changed. Could be group_size vs slab-frag interplay. What group_size was used for the pack build?

ana: group_size=64 for the new AWQ packs. Old baseline used 32. We moved to 64 to reduce quantization overhead and improve accuracy.

mike: accuracy tradeoff is good but packing overhead might ruin throughput. What about fallback kernel route? Are requests ending up on a slower kernel?

ana: routing logs show kernel selection picks the new awq-int8-group64 kernel, but there's an extra unpack stage that uses a generic path for cross-slab fragments. That path allocates temp buffers and triggers extra memcopy.

perf-bot: deploy-health: p99_latency +9% for model: redwood/llama-awq-int8 (canary) vs baseline.

sam: can you reproduce locally with microbench? try small seq len + hot KV set to measure prefetch hitrate.

ana: yes, I created a microbench harness — results:

```
micro: seq=64, batch=8, hotkeys=80%
baseline (group32): p99=180ms, kvcache_prefetch_hit=92%
awq-g64: p99=195ms, kvcache_prefetch_hit=76%, extra_unpacks=14%
```

chris: interesting. So prefetch hit drop is large. Maybe the pack alignment moved keys to different slab offsets causing predictor's stride pattern to break. Also group64 increases probability that a request spans a pack boundary.

mike: short-term mitigation: fallback policy to use group32 kernel for latency-sensitive routes or route to baseline kernel when prefetch hitrate < 85%. Can we do that quickly?

ana: I pushed a quick config override to canary routing to prefer group32 for chat-* routes. Observed immediate p99 drop back to baseline locally.

deploy-bot: canary routing config updated: prefer_kernel=awq-int8-group32 for route=chat-* (actor=ana).

sam: longer term: two action items — 1) adjust packer to preserve slab alignment invariant or emit slab-boundary hints for the prefetcher, 2) add a lightweight kvcache-prefetch telemetry counter so routing can make decisions without microbench.

chris: +1. Also consider adding a fast path unpack for cross-slab cases to avoid memcpy allocation.

mike: I can prototype an unpack fast-path that writes into preallocated scratch buffers and avoids heap alloc. Might cut extra_unpacks cost in half.

ana: plan:
- short: keep canary routing pinned to group32 for latency-critical routes (done)
- mid: perf prototype from mike for fast-path unpack (next 48h)
- mid: sam to add prefetch telemetry metric and route-level SLI (this week)
- long: evaluate packer changes to align groups to slab boundaries or emit prefetch hints (next sprint)

mike: will start on fast-path PR. tagging @sam for telemetry schema.

sam: on it. I'll add a new metric kvcache.prefetch_hit_rate and a tag pack_group_size so we can slice.

ana: thanks team. saving microbench logs to infra bucket and will attach to a follow-up thread with perf snapshots. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks — glad routing fallback gave immediate relief.

perf-bot: note: open issue #INFRA-827 created for AWQ packing prefetch regression (reporter=ana).

chris: we should also run calibrations with group32 vs 64 for AWQ to check quality delta. if accuracy loss is tiny, sticking with 32 for now is fine.

ana: agreed. I’ll run the calibration sweep with eval harness and post results.

mike: cool. keep updates in this thread.
_annot: Slack thread: short, engineering back-and-forth with microbench logs, profiling notes, and action items
